qt: to the Commission Dariusz Joński (PPE) Subject:

By its judgment of 24 September 2025 in Case T-354/24, the EU General Court annulled the provision limiting to 96 hours the time for which fishery products may be kept at a temperature suitable for slicing. The annulled restriction covered the entire temperature range between 0°C and −18°C, and thus all salmon slicing technologies. Following the judgment, the Commission commissioned EFSA to carry out a scientific assessment (mandate M-202500157). The Commission’s mandate sets out the scope of the scientific assessment to be carried out by EFSA. The assessment scenarios cover temperatures ranging from −12°C to −7°C, which are characteristic of hard slicing. Other temperature ranges were excluded from the scope, including those characteristic of soft slicing technology, carried out at temperatures ranging from approximately −5°C to approximately −2°C. The omission of temperature ranges which, according to RASFF data, are associated with a higher risk makes it difficult to assess differences in safety and to justify treating producers differently. In light of the above: 1.
Why has the Commission limited its mandate to temperatures specific to hard slicing, while omitting soft slicing used in the same sector?
Will the Commission expand the mandate to include a comparison of hard slicing and soft slicing, taking into account in both cases the subsequent 30-day storage period at +4°C, and if not, why?
Will the Commission rule out the introduction of restrictions applying exclusively to hard slicing without comparing the risks of both technologies and justifying a difference in treatment?
